title: Ἑρμῆς καὶ τεχνῖται
source: Émile Chambry, Ésope: Fables, texte établi et traduit (Les Belles Lettres, Paris, 1927), fable 111 (= Perry 103). Text as printed. Pronunciation: reconstructed Attic, after W. S. Allen, Vox Graeca. Romanization: standard classical transliteration (ē/ō; th/ph/ch; y for υ, u in diphthongs; h = rough breathing; ēi/āi/ōi for iota subscript; accents omitted).

sentences.t: Ζεὺς Ἑρμῇ προσέταξε πᾶσι τοῖς τεχνίταις ψεύδους φάρμακον χέαι.
sentences.tr: Zeus Hermēi prosetaxe pasi tois technitais pseudous pharmakon cheai.
sentences.l: Zeus ordered Hermes to pour a drug of falsehood into all the craftsmen.
sentences.n: φάρμακον is any prepared substance at all — drug, potion, poison, dye — and carries no judgement of its own; ψεύδους is a genitive of definition, the drug that consists in falsehood. The dative πᾶσι τοῖς τεχνίταις marks who receives it, as the compounds ἐνέχει and κατέχεεν below make plain.

sentences.t: Ὁ δὲ τοῦτο τρίψας καὶ μέτρον ποιήσας ἴσον ἑκάστῳ ἐνέχει.
sentences.tr: Ho de touto tripsas kai metron poiēsas ison hekastōi enechei.
sentences.l: And he, having ground this and having made an equal measure, went on pouring it in for each.
sentences.i: So he ground it up, made out an equal measure, and poured it into each of them.
sentences.n: τρίψας, from τρίβω, is the word for grinding a drug in a mortar. ἐνέχει is the imperfect of ἐγχέω: he went on pouring in, one craftsman after another.

sentences.t: Ἐπεὶ δέ, μόνου τοῦ σκυτέως ὑπολειφθέντος, πολὺ φάρμακον κατελείπετο, λαβὼν ὅλην τὴν χύσιν κατ’ αὐτοῦ κατέχεεν.
sentences.tr: Epei de, monou tou skyteōs hypoleiphthentos, poly pharmakon kateleipeto, labōn holēn tēn chysin kat’ autou katecheen.
sentences.l: But when, only the cobbler being left, much of the drug was left over, taking the whole outpouring he poured it down over him.
sentences.i: But when only the cobbler was left and a great deal of the drug still remained, he took the whole of it and emptied it over him.
sentences.n: μόνου τοῦ σκυτέως ὑπολειφθέντος is a genitive absolute. χύσις is the noun of χέω, the pouring or the mass poured out, and English has no single word for it. The joke sits in the prefixes: he had been pouring in, ἐν-έχει, measure by measure, and now pours down, κατ-έχεεν, all at once.

sentences.t: Ἐκ τούτου συνέβη τοὺς τεχνίτας πάντας ψεύδεσθαι, μάλιστα δὲ πάντων τοὺς σκυτέας.
sentences.tr: Ek toutou synebē tous technitas pantas pseudesthai, malista de pantōn tous skyteas.
sentences.l: From this it came about that all craftsmen lie, and most of all the cobblers.
sentences.n: συνέβη takes the accusative and infinitive, 'it came about that…'. The fable is an aetiology: a story invented to account for something already believed — that every trade lies, and the shoemakers' worst of all.

sentences.t: Πρὸς ἄνδρα ψευδολόγον ὁ λόγος εὔκαιρος.
sentences.tr: Pros andra pseudologon ho logos eukairos.
sentences.l: Against a man who speaks falsely the story is well-timed.
sentences.n: The same closing sentence as fable 55, with the words in the other order.
